topic: Scalable Field Kit control bar and slot-capacity progression
currentUserGoal: Replace the temporary text-button run-tool row with a scalable icon control bar, preserve room for many future systems and items, and gate additional equipped slots behind Memory progression.
workCompleted: Moved Tiny Sprinkler, Dew Pulse, and Root Salve out of the top status HUD into an icon-led Field Kit dock beside the playfield.
Added a shared RunToolCatalog for stable tool ids, original-game icon assets, colors, names, and player-facing descriptions.
Added stable square tool slots with RT cost badges, owned-count badges, ready/disabled presentation, hover/focus detail cards, restrained icon animation, and preserved SFX/action behavior.
Added a pure responsive Field Kit layout with two desktop columns, one narrow column, bounded four-row pages, and automatic previous/next navigation for future overflow.
Mirrored Field Kit slots, page navigation, previews, costs, counts, and readiness into the existing accessible DOM agent layer.
Added a save-compatible 30 GT Field Satchel Memory after Tiny Sprinkler. Runs begin with three equipped tool slots; Field Satchel adds three for a total capacity of six.
Added Field Satchel to the fixed Memory Grove world with original seed-satchel art, a non-crossing connector, dedicated copy, and per-node label offsets.
Shortened the main status HUD after removing its tool row, returning vertical space to the playfield while keeping objective, HP, currency, and Scourge lanes separate.
Stopped the active player card from listing every owned Memory name; mature saves now show a compact remembered-count while the full list remains in the Grove report.
Prevented focused transparent Field Kit DOM controls from painting accessibility text over their canvas icons while retaining a visible keyboard outline.
Updated the durable redesign and implementation-plan documents for the Field Kit, pagination, eleven-node Memory catalog, and slot-capacity progression.
verificationRun: Final npm run check passed: ESLint, 50 Vitest tests across six files, TypeScript, and the Vite production build.

New unit coverage verifies unique tool metadata/assets, desktop and narrow slot geometry, future ten-tool pagination, page clamping, Field Satchel prerequisites, +3 capacity effect, save round-tripping, and connector geometry.
Desktop browser smoke at 1280x720 restarted into one root, progressed to four active roots, exposed the Field Kit at 38 RT, and reported six equipped slots with Field Satchel owned.
The live Field Kit reported a stable two-column/two-row current-tool layout with no paging required for the three-tool catalog.

Dew Pulse browser smoke spent exactly 22 RT and reported lastRunToolKind dewPulse; Tiny Sprinkler then spent exactly 16 RT, incremented tinySprinklers to 1, and reported lastRunToolKind tinySprinkler.
Keyboard focus smoke verified the Dew Pulse DOM control retained a solid focus outline while its text, background, and text shadow remained visually transparent.
Browser screenshots covered the active Field Kit and the eleven-node Memory Grove with Field Satchel visible.
currentGitStatus: Expected after this handoff commit: clean worktree on codex/gameplay-update, four commits ahead of origin/codex/gameplay-update.
knownIssues: The current catalog contains exactly three run tools, so Field Satchel capacity is implemented and persisted but does not force a real loadout choice until a fourth tool arrives.
Overflow paging is covered by pure layout tests with a ten-tool future catalog but cannot yet be exercised through live gameplay.
Field Satchel cost, position, and +3 value are first-pass progression tuning and need hands-on feedback alongside natural GT earnings.
This browser runtime remained fixed at 1280x720, so the one-column 390px Field Kit layout was unit-tested but not screenshot-smoked.
The compact remembered-count correction was made after the final live screenshot; it passed the full static/test/build gate but was not recaptured before browser finalization.
nextRecommendedSteps: Have the user play a natural run and judge the Field Kit's size, placement, icon readability, tooltip timing, and whether the shorter HUD gives the field enough breathing room.
Design the fourth run tool or item so Field Satchel becomes an immediate loadout decision rather than future scaffolding.
Define the eventual equip/loadout screen only when the catalog exceeds capacity; do not add inventory management before there is a meaningful choice.
Tune Field Satchel cost against the current Tiny Sprinkler branch and natural permanent-GT pacing.
Re-run a 390x844 Field Kit screenshot when a resizable browser surface is available.
doNotRevert: Do not put run tools back into the top status HUD as wide text buttons.
Keep tool presentation in RunToolCatalog and layout math in RunToolBarLayout instead of adding new per-tool scene branches for future items.
Keep tool unlocks separate from equipped-slot capacity: base capacity is three and Field Satchel adds three.
Keep the Field Kit hidden during the one-tile opening and reveal each tool only when its gameplay condition matters.
Keep the transparent DOM controls and readable debug state aligned with every visible Field Kit action.
Every new run must still return to one tile at mastery rank 0 while permanent GT, Memory upgrades, and Field Satchel capacity survive.
